🌐 BigCommerce

Managing the Port Store website. Use BigCommerce for visibility, channels, categories, orders and customers. Product content (names, descriptions, images, prices) is managed in Lightspeed and syncs across automatically.

⇄️
Lightspeed syncs one way into BigCommerce
Product names, descriptions, images and prices set in Lightspeed will overwrite BigCommerce on each sync. Only use BigCommerce to manage visibility, channels and categories. Changes to product content made directly in BC will be lost on the next sync.
📍 How to get to products
BC Admin → Products → View
Use the search bar to find by name or SKU. Click the product name to open the editor.
1
Find the product
Go to Products → View. Use the search bar to find by name or SKU. Click the product name (blue link) to open the editor.
2
Set storefront visibility & publish to channels
New products from Lightspeed may not be visible by default. Both settings must be correct for customers to see the product.
👁️ Enable storefront visibility
Scroll to Storefront in the product editor. Tick Visible on storefront. If unticked, customers cannot see the product regardless of channel settings.
Product editor → Storefront → tick Visible on storefront
🔗 Publish to channels
Find the Channels section in the product editor. Make sure the product is enabled on all relevant storefronts - typically the Port Store channel.
Product editor → Channels → tick all relevant storefronts
💡 A product can be Enabled in status but still invisible if storefront visibility is off or it isn’t published to a channel. Both must be correct.
⚠️ If a Lightspeed sync runs after you make visibility changes, check these settings haven’t been reset.
3
Save your changes
Scroll to the bottom and click Save. Changes go live immediately.
⚠️ Product edits go live immediately on save. Double-check before saving.

Categories are what BigCommerce uses in the navigation to group products. The dropdowns and main links in the navigation bar are all categories. Here’s how to create and manage them.

📁 Creating & editing categories
1
Navigate to Categories
From the BC Admin home page, go to the Products dropdown in the left sidebar and select Categories.
BC Admin → Products → Categories
The Categories page - existing categories listed on the left
2
Create a new category or sub-category
To create a top-level category, click Create a Category. To create a sub-category under an existing one, click the three dots to the right of the parent category and select Create Sub Category.
The new category panel - only the name is required
💡 You only need to enter the category name and click Save & Edit. This takes you to another page - just click Save again and the category is created.
3
Assign products to the new category
There are two ways to add products to a category - from the individual product page, or by selecting multiple products at once from the product list.
📄 Single product
Open the product editor, scroll to the Categories section, tick the category and save. Multiple categories can be selected.
Product editor → Categories → tick → Save
✅ Multiple products at once
Select products using the checkboxes on the right of the product list. Click the three dots next to the Actions button and choose Add to Categories. Categories are listed under the first sales channel - Port Store.
Products → View → tick products → … → Add to Categories
Selecting multiple products and using the three dots menu to add to categories
💡 If a product isn’t showing on a collection page, check the correct category is ticked and the product is saved.
👤 Making new categories visible to all customers
⚠️ Because Port Store has member-exclusive products, new categories are not automatically visible to all customers. You must update customer group access for each new category you create.
1
Navigate to Customer Groups
Go to Customers → Customer Groups in the BC Admin sidebar.
BC Admin → Customers → Customer Groups
Customer Groups - update Normal and Not Current Member one at a time
2
Edit the “Normal” customer group
Click on the Normal customer group to open it. In the Group Access section, click the search icon. This pulls up a list of all categories - find and select the new category to add it to the group’s access.
Search for the new category in Group Access and select it
💡 Save the customer group once you’ve added the category.
3
Repeat for “Not Current Member”
Go back to Customer Groups and repeat the same process for the Not Current Member group. Both groups need to be updated separately for the category to be visible to all non-member customers.

Gift certificates can be purchased online and redeemed at any of our 3 outlets.

🔎 Finding gift certificates
1
Navigate to Orders - Gift Certificates
From the BC Admin sidebar, go to Orders then select Gift Certificates.
BC Admin - Orders - Gift Certificates
2
Sort by date and view details
BigCommerce randomly sorts gift certificates by default. To sort by date, click Date Purchased twice to get them in order (newest first). To view the details of a gift certificate, click the plus icon on the left-hand side of the row.
3
Resend a gift certificate
If a customer needs their gift certificate resent, click the three dots to the right of the gift certificate and select Resend.
📝 Important notes
⚠️ You cannot update or change customer details or email addresses once a gift certificate has been issued, even if they were entered incorrectly.
🎨 Manual gift certificate
If a customer can't receive their gift certificate email for any reason, edit the Canva template with the correct details, export as an image and send it to them directly.

📋 Lightspeed

Lightspeed is the source of truth for all product content. Changes made here sync automatically into BigCommerce. Always start here when creating or updating products.

⇄️
Lightspeed syncs one way into BigCommerce - not back
Product names, descriptions, images and prices set here will overwrite BigCommerce on each sync. Changes made directly in BigCommerce to these fields will be lost. Always make product content changes here first.

Stage 1 - Prepare the file
📥
Download the template
Always start from the Port Store template. Column names must match exactly - don’t rename or add columns.
📥 Download Lightspeed Upload Template
📄
One row per variant
Each size gets its own row. Product name, category, prices, brand and supplier repeat on every row - only SKU, barcode and size change per row.
ℹ️
Products with no variants still get one row - leave variant_option_one_name and variant_option_one_value blank.
💾
Save as CSV UTF-8
Save using File → Save As → CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited).
⚠️
Don’t use “CSV (MS-DOS)” - it breaks special characters on import.
✔️
Quick checks before you save
🔢 Barcode column formatted as Text - prevents 8.05E+12
📷 Every row has a unique sku_code_custom
💰 Prices are numbers only - no $ symbols
📝 Product names identical across all rows for the same product
📷 Tags semicolon-separated: 2026 Macron Range;2026 SDNR
Stage 2 - Column reference
💡
Column headers are case-sensitive. Copy directly from the template - don’t rename them.
tax_name
Default Tax
active

product_categoryRequiredMust match existing Lightspeed category exactly.AFL (MACRON) / Guernseys

Stage 3 - Add barcodes (Macron products)
💡
This step is Macron-specific. Macron sends barcodes in a separate document in a different format. Use a VLOOKUP to match them to your products before importing. Skip this step for non-Macron ranges.
Three files you need
📋 Lightspeed upload
Your product list - the file that ultimately needs the barcodes
📝 Macron order form
Your edited version with Port Store naming convention
🔢 Macron barcode list
The separate file Macron sends with the barcodes (Col E: Article, Col F: Size)
📄
Add Port Store names to the barcode spreadsheet
Open the Macron barcode file. You will be using Col E (Article) and Col F (Size).
The Macron barcode file - Article in Col E, Size in Col F
Insert a new column between Article (Col E) and Size (Col F). Title it Port Store Name.
ℹ️
The Macron order form often has hidden columns (e.g. Col F jumps to Col K). Unhide them, then delete them so the Macron name and Port Store name columns sit directly next to each other - the VLOOKUP needs this.
Macron order form - hidden columns must be unhidden and deleted so columns are adjacent
In the first cell of the Port Store Name column, type =VLOOKUP( and click the Article column (Col E) to use as the lookup value. Navigate to the edited Macron order form and drag across the two columns (Macron name and Port Store name). End with , 2, 0) and press Enter. Your formula bar should look like this:
VLOOKUP formula referencing the Macron order form
Port Store Name column filling in from the VLOOKUP
Drag the formula down the full column, then copy and paste as values.
⚠️
Items that don’t match will show as #N/A or 0 - usually SANFL or PRO items. Remove rows you aren’t working with from the barcode file.
🔗
Create a "Port Store Name & Size" column in both files
In the barcode sheet, add a new column called Port Store Name & Size. Use a concatenation formula to combine the name and size:
=(Port Store Name cell)&"-"&(Size cell)
Concatenation formula: =F2&"-"&G2 combining name and size
Drag the formula down the full column, then copy and paste as values. The result should look like this:
Port Store Name & Size column created - name and size combined with a hyphen
Repeat the same process in your Lightspeed upload file - create the same Port Store Name & Size column so both files have an identical matching key. Your completed barcode sheet with barcodes should look like this:
Completed barcode sheet with Port Store Name & Size and EAN columns ready
🔁
VLOOKUP barcodes into the Lightspeed file
In your Lightspeed upload file, ensure you have a Port Store Name & Size column and a blank sku_code_barcode column ready. It should look like this:
Lightspeed upload file with Port Store Name & Size column and blank sku_code_barcode column
In the Macron barcode file, make sure the Port Store Name & Size column is directly to the left of the barcode (EAN) column.
In the first cell of sku_code_barcode in your Lightspeed file, type =VLOOKUP( and click your Port Store Name & Size column as the lookup value. Navigate to the Macron barcode file and drag across the Port Store Name & Size and EAN columns. End with , 2, 0) and press Enter. Your formula bar should look like this:
VLOOKUP formula in the sku_code_barcode column referencing the Macron barcode file
Drag the formula down the full column, then copy and paste as values. The completed file should look like this:
Completed Lightspeed upload with barcodes matched in from the Macron barcode file
✅
Your Lightspeed upload file now has barcodes matched in. Proceed to Stage 4 to run the import.
Stage 4 - Run the import
⚠️
Test first. Run a small file of 5–10 products before your full upload.
💻
Navigate to the import tool
Products›Import / Export›Import Products
☑️
Select import type
Choose Add new products for a new range.
🚫
Don’t use “Update existing” for a new range - rows with no existing match are silently skipped.
📤
Upload CSV and confirm mapping
Click Choose File, select your CSV, then Next. Manually assign anything showing “Not mapped”.
▶️
Run the import
Click Import and don’t navigate away. Any skips above zero need investigating.
Troubleshooting
⚠️ Rows being skipped with no error
Usually a column mapping issue or wrong import type. Check headers match the template exactly and confirm you chose Add new products.
🔢 Barcodes show as scientific notation (8.05E+12)
The barcode column is formatted as a number. Select the column, format as Text, re-paste barcodes as values, then re-export the CSV.
📄 Duplicate products instead of variants
A variant row has a slightly different product name - even a trailing space causes Lightspeed to create a new product. Use Excel find-replace to standardise.
📁 Category not found
Category name doesn’t exactly match Lightspeed. Pull the exact name from Products → Categories in Back Office.
💰 Prices show as $0.00 after import
Price columns contain a $ symbol or comma. Remove with find-replace, re-export, then re-import using Update existing products.

Use this method when adding one or a small number of products directly in Lightspeed Back Office.

1
Navigate to Products
In Lightspeed Back Office, go to Products in the left sidebar, then click New Product.
Back Office - Products - New Product
2
Enter the product details
Fill in the core product fields. These sync directly to BigCommerce so get them right here first.
FieldNotes
NameFull product name - must be identical across all variant rows
DescriptionProduct description shown on the website - syncs to BC
CategoryMust match an existing Lightspeed category exactly
BrandUsed for filtering in Back Office
SupplierRequired if using purchase orders
Retail priceIncl. GST - numbers only, no $ symbol
Supply priceEx-GST cost price
SKUUnique per variant - no spaces
BarcodeEAN-13 - format as Text to prevent scientific notation
3
Add variants (if sized)
If the product comes in multiple sizes, add each as a variant under the same product. Each variant gets its own SKU, barcode and stock level. Use Size as the variant option name.
💡 Keep the product name identical across all variants - even a trailing space will create a duplicate product.
4
Upload images
Add product images here in Lightspeed - they will sync through to BigCommerce automatically. Don’t upload images directly in BC as they’ll be overwritten on the next sync.
5
Save the product
Click Save. The product is now in Lightspeed and ready to publish to BigCommerce - see the Publishing to BigCommerce section below.

Use Lightspeed for all product content changes. These fields sync to BigCommerce - editing them in BC directly will be overwritten on the next sync.

FieldWhere to editNotes
Product nameLightspeedMust be identical across all variant rows. Syncs to BC.
DescriptionLightspeedSyncs to BC - don’t edit in BC
ImagesLightspeedUpload here - syncs to BC. Don’t upload directly in BC.
Price & sale priceLightspeedNumbers only, no $ symbol. Syncs to BC.
Stock levelsLightspeedManaged here, synced to BC.
SKU / barcodeLightspeedDon’t change SKU without checking inventory impact.
Category (LS)LightspeedBack Office filtering only - separate from BC category pages.
VisibilityBigCommerceSet in BC - not affected by sync.
BC CategoriesBigCommerceWhich collection pages the product appears on - set in BC.
ChannelsBigCommerceWhich storefronts the product is published to - set in BC.
💡 Quick rule: if it affects how a product looks on the website, edit it in Lightspeed. If it affects where or whether it appears, edit it in BigCommerce.

Once a product is ready in Lightspeed, follow these steps to push it across to BigCommerce.

1
Navigate to the Products page in Lightspeed
Open Lightspeed Back Office and go to the Products section.
2
Press the “Publish to BigCommerce” pill
Under the product, there is a grey pill labelled Publish to BigCommerce. Click it to push the product across. This usually takes around 30 seconds.
3
Confirm it’s live - pill turns green
Once complete, the pill will turn green and change to View on BigCommerce. You can click it to go directly to the product on the storefront.
4
Check the product in BigCommerce
Navigate to Products → View in BC Admin - the newly published product should appear at the top of the list. From here you can set visibility, categories and channels.
BC Admin → Products → View
💡 New products may not be visible to customers by default - see BigCommerce → Products for visibility and channel steps.

Use this process when you don’t have a Lightspeed CSV, or want to create the AWDS Product Advice file manually from the AWDS template.

1
Download the AWDS template
Always use the Port Store AWDS template. Column names and order must match exactly.
📥 Download AWDS Product Template
2
Fill in the columns
One row per variant. The template has 6 columns:
ColumnWhat to enter
ProductCodeUnique SKU per variant (from sku_code_custom in Lightspeed)
DescriptionProduct name - must be identical across all variant rows
ProductGroupAlways MERCH
ItemsPerOuterAlways 100
OutersPerPalletAlways 100
ItemBarcodeEAN-13 barcode - format column as Text to prevent scientific notation
⚠️ Format the ItemBarcode column as Text before entering barcodes - otherwise Excel converts them to scientific notation (e.g. 8.88E+11).
3
Save as CSV UTF-8
File → Save As → CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited). Name the file: YYYYMMDD_RangeName_AWDS_Product_Advice.csv
4
Email to Alex Perry
Send the completed CSV to AWDS.

Process
1
Fill out the Virtue onboarding form
Submit through Virtue’s onboarding form with the settings shown on the left. Attach the Item & Shot List template.
2
Wait for confirmation & VC- order number
Virtue will reply by email with a job confirmation. The order number starts with VC- (e.g. VC-1623) - keep this for reference.
3
Pack items with a completed packing slip
Pack the garments and include a completed packing slip. Usually send a Medium or Large size for ghost mannequin shoots.
4
Ship via TNT or Australia Post
Send to the Virtue studio address shown on the left.
5
Monitor for updates during shoot & edit
Virtue will send email updates throughout the process. No action needed - just monitor your inbox.
6
Receive completed imagery via Google Drive
Once complete, Virtue emails a Google Drive link with the final imagery. Download and save to the SharePoint folder.
7
Send return shipping label to Virtue
Generate a return label for the garments and email it to team@virtuecreative.com.au

How to publish this to BigCommerce
The category must be active and visible before you can add a header - hidden categories won’t appear in Page Builder
1
Generate and copy your category header code
Use the generator above to enter the category name, click Generate, then Copy Code.
⚠️ The category must be active and visible before continuing. If the category isn’t showing on the storefront yet, enable visibility first - see BigCommerce → Products → Visibility.
2
Open the category in Page Builder
Go to Products → Categories. Find your category, click the three dots on the right and select View in Page Builder.
BC Admin → Products → Categories → … → View in Page Builder
Three dots menu → View in Page Builder
3
Drag a Layout module to the top of the page
In Page Builder, find the Layout module in the left panel and drag it to the very top of the page - above the existing content.
Drag Layout to top of page
4
Change the layout to 1 column
The layout will default to 2 columns. Click it to select it and change to 1 column.
Change from 2 columns to 1 column
5
Drag an HTML module inside the layout
From the left panel, drag an HTML module into the single-column layout you just created.
Drag HTML module into the layout column
6
Paste your code and publish
Click the HTML module to open it, paste your copied code, and click Apply. Then click Publish in the top right to make it live.
Paste code → click Apply → click Publish
💡 Repeat this process for each new category - the layout and HTML module only need to be added once per category page.
💬 Customer Service Procedures
AWDS Fulfilment · Online Orders · Internal Reference
📍
Address Issues
Flagged by AWDS when a delivery address can’t be resolved
ℹ️
AWDS will contact you directly when they can’t deliver to an address - typically the suburb, city or postcode was entered incorrectly at checkout.
1
Google the address
Take the street number and name from the order and search Google Maps to confirm the correct suburb and postcode. Resolves most cases without contacting the customer.
2
If you can’t confirm - email the customer
Ask the customer to confirm their full delivery address including suburb and postcode.
📧 Suggested email
Hi [Name], We’re getting in touch regarding your recent Port Store order. Our fulfilment team has encountered an issue with the delivery address we have on file. Could you please confirm your full delivery address - including street, suburb and postcode - so we can get your order on its way? Thanks, Port Store Team
3
Update in BigCommerce and notify AWDS
Once confirmed, update the shipping address on the order in BigCommerce and pass the corrected details back to AWDS so they can proceed with dispatch.
✈️
International Orders & Tracking
Tracking numbers don’t automatically appear in BigCommerce for international orders
⚠️
Expected behaviour - not a system error. The customer receives a dispatch confirmation but without tracking. Must be sourced manually from AWDS.
1
Customer asks where their tracking is
When an international customer contacts you about missing tracking, follow this process.
2
Reach out to Steve & Rebecca at AWDS with the order number
AP
Alex Perry
aperry@awds.com.au
3
Forward the tracking number to the customer
Once AWDS provides it, send the tracking number to the customer via email.
📦
Stock Issues
When AWDS can’t fulfil an item - process differs based on order size
💡
Always check before adjusting inventory. If the system shows 2+ units in stock but AWDS is showing zero, ask AWDS to do a physical stock check before making any Lightspeed changes.
Single item order - AWDS can’t fulfil the item
1
Ask AWDS to remove the order from their system
2
Fulfil from Alberton - Samuel adds tracking in BigCommerce
Pick and dispatch from Alberton Oval. Samuel will enter the tracking number into BigCommerce once sent.
3
Transfer stock from Online to Alberton in Lightspeed
⚠️
System shows 1 in stock (Online)
Remove this unit from the Online location in Lightspeed - it’s being fulfilled from Alberton.
🔍
System shows 2+ but AWDS has zero
Ask AWDS for a physical stock check before making any changes.
Two item order - one item can’t be fulfilled by AWDS
💡
Use your judgment based on the value difference between the two items. The goal is always the best outcome for the customer.
1
Assess which item is unavailable
🥽
High-value item unavailable (e.g. jacket)
Email the customer and ask how they’d like to proceed. They likely won’t want to pay full shipping for just a keyring.
🔑
Low-value item unavailable (e.g. keyring)
Email to advise you’ve refunded the unavailable item and dispatched the main item. Refund in BigCommerce.
2
Adjust inventory in Lightspeed if needed
🔍
System shows 2+ but AWDS has zero
Ask AWDS for a physical stock check before adjusting. Transfer Online to Alberton once confirmed.
Three or more item order - one item can’t be fulfilled by AWDS
1
Email the customer - notify and refund the unavailable item
📧 Suggested email
Hi [Name], Thank you for your recent Port Store order. Unfortunately we’re unable to fulfil [item name] as it’s no longer available. We’ve processed a refund of [amount] back to your original payment method - this should appear within 3–5 business days. The rest of your order has been dispatched and you’ll receive tracking shortly. Thanks, Port Store Team
2
Tell AWDS to ship the remainder of the order
3
Adjust inventory in Lightspeed
⚠️
System shows 1 in stock (Online)
Remove from the Online location in Lightspeed.
🔍
System shows 2+ but AWDS has zero
Ask AWDS for a physical stock check first.
❌
Cancelling Orders
We don’t officially offer cancellations, but we try to help wherever possible
⚠️
Policy reminder: Our website states we do not facilitate cancellations. That said, always try to assist - the earlier the request, the more likely AWDS can hold the order before packing.
1
Contact Steve & Rebecca at AWDS immediately
Email AWDS with the order number and ask whether it’s been packed yet.
AP
Alex Perry
aperry@awds.com.au
2
Respond to the customer based on AWDS’s answer
✅ Not yet packed - can cancel
Confirm cancellation to the customer. Cancel in BigCommerce and process any applicable refund.
🚚 Already dispatched - can’t cancel
Advise the customer the order is already on its way. Direct to returns process if needed.
🔍
Missing Orders & Postal Issues
When a customer says their order hasn’t arrived
1
Check tracking in BigCommerce before responding
Look up the order and review the tracking status. In many cases the parcel has been delivered to the customer’s local post office and they haven’t been notified.
💡
A “delivered” scan at a nearby post office is the most common cause. Let the customer know to check their local post office with ID before escalating.
2
If delivered but not received - escalate to AWDS
AWDS hold the Australia Post account and must manage all postal investigations on our behalf.
🚫
Do not contact Australia Post directly - AWDS must manage all postal enquiries and investigations on our behalf.
SA
Alex Perry
aperry@awds.com.au
↩️
Returns
Ecommerce returns managed via AWDS warehouse
ℹ️
AWDS manage all ecommerce returns at the warehouse and will email you with a list of items received. They also log returns directly into the shared register.
1
AWDS receive the return & email you a list
When returned parcels arrive at the AWDS warehouse, they email you with a list of items received and log them in the shared returns register. AWDS automatically return the stock to their system at this point.
📊 View Returns Register
2
Refund the order in BigCommerce & change status to Refunded
Go through the list of returns from AWDS and for each one: process the refund in BigCommerce and update the order status to Refunded.
⚠️
Stock won’t be available to customers until you complete this step. Even though AWDS have returned the item to their system, it won’t appear as available stock in Lightspeed until the return is processed on our side in BigCommerce.
